findings.title: Mutable default timestamp evaluated once at import
findings.body: File src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py line 18 defines `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` as a dataclass default. This calls `timezone.now()` once at import time, so every AssignmentSource instance created without an explicit `queued` shares the same timestamp. It should use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)`. Consequence is all sources carry a stale identical queued time, breaking any ordering/debounce logic and the test expectation of freshness.

findings.title: to_dict emits non-JSON-serializable datetime for Celery
findings.body: File src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py `to_dict()` returns `asdict(self)` including the raw `datetime queued`. File src/sentry/integrations/utils/sync.py passes that dict as `assignment_source_dict` into `sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async(kwargs=...)` which must be JSON-serializable for Celery. A datetime payload fails serialization / deserialization, so outbound sync tasks will fail or be lost. After JSON round-trip `from_dict` would also receive a string for `queued` and store a str where datetime is expected, with no ISO parsing.

findings.title: Passing unexpected assignment_source kwarg to installations
findings.body: File src/sentry/integrations/tasks/sync_assignee_outbound.py line 59 calls `installation.sync_assignee_outbound(..., assignment_source=parsed_assignment_source)` but the abstract in src/sentry/integrations/mixins/issues.py defines `sync_assignee_outbound(self, external_issue, user, assign=True, **kwargs)` without an explicit parameter, and concrete integrations are not updated. Any concrete `sync_assignee_outbound` without `**kwargs` or explicit `assignment_source` will raise TypeError at runtime. Tests mock the method so the break is hidden. Consequence is outbound assignee sync crashes for real providers.

findings.title: Invalid source dict fails open and re-creates sync loop
findings.body: File src/sentry/integrations/tasks/sync_assignee_outbound.py lines 53-56 parse `assignment_source_dict` with `AssignmentSource.from_dict` which returns None on ValueError/TypeError, then calls `should_sync(..., None)`. A malformed or version-skewed dict therefore degrades to no-source and syncs to the originating integration, re-creating the exact assignee sync cycle this PR claims to fix. It should fail closed (skip) or log when a dict was provided but unparseable.
